iterations.theme: Marko Matijašević: identitet, udruga Eho, liderstvo, osvajanje supruge, bračni život i financije u braku

sections.subtitle: Prvo muž i otac, a tek onda sve ostalo
sections.screenshot_description: Marko Matijašević odgovara na pitanje tko je on kad se zanemari njegov posao
sections.content:
Epizoda podcasta **Redefinicija** počinje provokativnim isječkom. Gost tvrdi da novcem u braku treba upravljati sposobniji partner, a ne nužno muškarac. *„Ima muškaraca koji ne znaju upravljati novcima. Ako je žena sposobnija, daj njoj da upravlja novcima“*, kaže **Marko Matijašević**. Dodaje da supruga ne bi trebala šutke gledati kako muž „srlja i radi gluposti“ samo zato što je on glava obitelji: *„Preuzmi ih nazad. Inače ćete biti u problemima.“*

Nakon pozdrava „Hvaljen Isus i Marija, i sveti Josip“ voditelj **Krunoslav** predstavlja gosta kao predsjednika udruge Eho, koja vodi niz zanimljivih projekata. Prije razgovora o udruzi Krunoslav postavlja pitanje koje i sam naziva „prefilozofskim“: tko je Marko Matijašević kad ne spominje ono čime se bavi?

Marko odgovara bez puno razmišljanja. *„Prvo sam muž i otac. Mislim, stvarno jesam. Nakon toga sam sve ovo ostalo čime se bavim.“* Priznaje da je teško odvojiti ono što čovjek radi od vlastitog identiteta. U posljednje vrijeme o tome često razmišlja i to naziva **zamkom**: ljudi se poistovjećuju s onim što rade i na tome grade osjećaj vlastite vrijednosti. Na kraju se opisuje redom: muž, otac, teolog, voditelj.

Krunoslav ocjenjuje da je gost odgovorom rekao mnogo. Ljudi se obično predstavljaju zanimanjem, što pokazuje da im je posao identitet i prvo mjesto na ljestvici prioriteta. Kad su na prvom mjestu supružnik i obitelj, smatra Krunoslav, sve ostalo dođe na svoje mjesto. Dodaje i ogradu da Bog uvijek treba biti prvi, a ova se ljestvica odnosi na ostale prioritete. Odgovor proglašava „jako zadovoljavajućim“, a Marko se našali da je „prošao“.
sections.subtitle_en: First a husband and father, and only then everything else
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko Matijašević answers the question of who he is when his work is disregarded
sections.content_en:
The episode of the **Redefinicija** podcast begins with a provocative clip. The guest claims that money in marriage should be managed by the more capable partner, and not necessarily the man. *„There are men who do not know how to manage money. If the woman is more capable, let her manage the money”*, says **Marko Matijašević**. He adds that a wife should not silently watch her husband „rush ahead and do foolish things“ just because he is the head of the family: *„Take it back. Otherwise you will be in trouble.“*

After the greeting „Praised be Jesus and Mary, and Saint Joseph“, host **Krunoslav** introduces the guest as the president of udruga Eho, which leads a series of interesting projects. Before the conversation about the association, Krunoslav asks a question that he himself calls „too philosophical“: who is Marko Matijašević when he does not mention what he does?

Marko answers without much thought. *„First I am a husband and father. I mean, I really am. After that, I am all this other stuff I do.“* He admits that it is difficult to separate what a person does from one's own identity. Lately he has often been thinking about this and calls it a **trap**: people identify with what they do and build a sense of self-worth on that. In the end, he describes himself in order: husband, father, theologian, leader.

Krunoslav assesses that the guest said a lot with his answer. People usually introduce themselves by their profession, which shows that their job is their identity and first place on the scale of priorities. When spouse and family are in first place, Krunoslav believes, everything else falls into place. He also adds the qualification that God should always be first, and this scale refers to the other priorities. He declares the answer „very satisfying“, and Marko jokes that he „passed“.

sections.subtitle: Udruga Eho: pet pouka iz Tobijine knjige kao temelj
sections.screenshot_description: Marko objašnjava kako je Tobitova oporuka sinu Tobiji postala temelj programa udruge
sections.content:
Na pitanje čime se udruga Eho bavi, Marko najprije objašnjava neobičan naziv **Eho projekt**. Domena *eho.hr* bila je zauzeta, pa je trebalo nešto dodati. Budući da je udruga imala više projekata, dodali su riječ „projekt“.

U suštini je riječ o **molitvenoj zajednici** kojoj su svrha **evangelizacija i odgoj vjernika**. Sve što rade usmjereno je na pitanje kako vjernici svoja uvjerenja žive u svakodnevnom životu. Polazište je bila **Tobijina knjiga**, odnosno trenutak kad Tobit, misleći da će umrijeti, sinu Tobiji ostavlja pet važnih pouka:

- **Obitelj:** da se nastavi brinuti za majku i čuva obiteljske odnose.
- **Molitva i odnos prema Bogu:** da ne zaboravi moliti i nastavi s onim što su i prije činili.
- **Novac:** da ne zaboravi svoje sugrađane i da ne prestane davati.
- **Odnos prema radnicima:** sažet u rečenici *„Neka ničija plaća ne prenoći kod tebe.“* U njoj Marko prepoznaje temelj liderstva, poduzetništva i utjecaja.
- **Partnerski odnosi:** da žena ne bude iz tuđeg, nego iz njegova roda.

Tih pet točaka bilo je početni okvir, a danas se udruga znatno proširila. Marko procjenjuje da je u posljednje vrijeme aktivno bilo više od deset programa. Svima je zajednički cilj pokazati ljudima kako njihova vjera funkcionira u partnerskim odnosima, financijama, braku, odnosu prema poslu te u molitvi i duhovnosti.
sections.subtitle_en: Udruga Eho: five lessons from the Book of Tobit as a foundation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko explains how Tobit's testament to his son Tobiah became the foundation of the association's programs
sections.content_en:
When asked what Udruga Eho does, Marko first explains the unusual name **Eho projekt**. The domain *eho.hr* was taken, so something needed to be added. Since the association had multiple projects, they added the word “project”.

Essentially, it is a **prayer community** whose purpose is the **evangelization and formation of believers**. Everything they do is directed toward the question of how believers live out their beliefs in everyday life. The starting point was the **Book of Tobit**, specifically the moment when Tobit, thinking he is about to die, leaves five important lessons to his son Tobiah:

- **Family:** to continue caring for his mother and preserve family relationships.
- **Prayer and relationship with God:** not to forget to pray and to continue with what they had been doing before.
- **Money:** not to forget his fellow countrymen and not to stop giving.
- **Relationship with workers:** summarized in the sentence *“Let no one's wages stay overnight with you.”* In it, Marko recognizes the foundation of leadership, entrepreneurship, and influence.
- **Partner relationships:** that his wife not be from a foreign clan, but from his own lineage.

Those five points were the initial framework, and today the association has expanded considerably. Marko estimates that more than ten programs have been active recently. They all share the common goal of showing people how their faith functions in partner relationships, finances, marriage, attitude toward work, and in prayer and spirituality.

sections.subtitle: Od predškolaca do studenata: ostvareni san zvan Eho Kids
sections.screenshot_description: Marko s oduševljenjem govori o projektu Eho Kids za djecu od tri do šest godina
sections.content:
Osim edukativnih programa, udruga organizira **duhovne obnove, evangelizaciju i rad s mladima**: sa srednjoškolcima, studentima, starijima i djecom. Marko naglašava da je raspon „širok“.

Poseban mu je ponos projekt **Eho Kids**, namijenjen predškolcima od tri do šest godina. Krunoslav primjećuje da je to „jako zanimljiva ekipa“. Marko priznaje da mu je taj projekt „najviše na srcu ležao“ i da je bio presretan kad su ga prošle godine pokrenuli, jer je to bio njegov san posljednjih četiri do pet godina. Nada se da će se projekt nastaviti.

Unatoč brojnim projektima, cilj ostaje isti: *„odgoj vjernika i to oduševljavanje za Krista i praktično to držanje“*.
sections.subtitle_en: From preschoolers to university students: a dream come true called Eho Kids
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko speaks with enthusiasm about the Eho Kids project for children aged three to six
sections.content_en:
In addition to educational programs, the association organizes **spiritual retreats, evangelization, and work with youth**: with high schoolers, university students, older people, and children. Marko emphasizes that the range is "wide".

A special point of pride for him is the **Eho Kids** project, intended for preschoolers from three to six years old. Krunoslav remarks that this is "a very interesting crew". Marko admits that this project "lay closest to his heart" and that he was overjoyed when they launched it last year, because it had been his dream for the last four to five years. He hopes that the project will continue.

Despite numerous projects, the goal remains the same: *"the formation of believers and inspiring enthusiasm for Christ and practically holding to that"*.

sections.subtitle: Eho konferencija, Probudi i konferencija za žene
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Krunoslav spominje Eho konferenciju, a Marko najavljuje sljedeće izdanje u Mozaik Event Centru
sections.content:
Krunoslav ističe **Eho konferenciju** koja se održava gotovo svake godine. Marko ga ispravlja: održava se **svake godine**. Sljedeća će biti 13. prosinca u **Mozaik Event Centru**, a riječ je, kako kaže, vjerojatno o četrnaestom izdanju. Prva je održana 2014., prije jedanaest godina, dok je ekipa još bila dio **Zajednice Dobri pastir**.

Tada nastalo ime ostalo je i nakon osamostaljenja. Marko objašnjava da je Eho dio njegove osobne vizije i identiteta koji je zadržao. Ideja je da *„sve što radimo odjekne“*.

Eho konferencija je glavni događaj u godini, ali nije jedini:

- **Probudi**, konferencija za srednjoškolce i studente, koju Marko opisuje kao „najhajpaniju“, „napucanu“ i „snažnu“ za tu generaciju;
- **konferencija za žene**;
- povremena dodatna događanja tijekom godine, „što se već sjetimo i ubacimo“.

Krunoslav zaključuje da je to iznimno mnogo projekata za udrugu koju još uvijek smatra mladom.
sections.subtitle_en: Eho conference, Probudi, and conference for women
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Krunoslav mentions the Eho conference, and Marko announces the next edition at the Mozaik Event Centar
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav highlights the **Eho conference**, which is held almost every year. Marko corrects him: it is held **every year**. The next one will be on December 13 at the **Mozaik Event Centar**, and it is, as he says, probably the fourteenth edition. The first was held in 2014, eleven years ago, while the team was still part of the **Zajednica Dobri pastir**.

The name created back then remained even after becoming independent. Marko explains that Eho is part of his personal vision and identity that he retained. The idea is that *"everything we do echoes"*.

The Eho conference is the main event of the year, but it is not the only one:

- **Probudi**, a conference for high school and university students, which Marko describes as "the most hyped", "pumped-up", and "powerful" for that generation;
- **conference for women**;
- occasional additional events throughout the year, "whatever we think of and throw in".

Krunoslav concludes that this is an exceptionally large number of projects for an association he still considers young.

sections.subtitle: Kad je lider dobro, svi dobivaju
sections.screenshot_description: Marko citira rečenicu s GLS-a o tome da od dobrog stanja lidera koristi imaju svi
sections.content:
Krunoslav prelazi na temu koja se provlači kroz projekte udruge: **liderstvo muškarca**. Podsjeća da su se često susretali na GLS-ovima i da Marko o tome redovito govori na konferencijama. Pita ga zašto je danas važno da se muškarac pokrene kao lider.

Marko odgovara rečenicom koju je čuo na GLS-u: *„Kad je lider dobro, svi dobivaju.“* Ne zna je li riječ o sloganu ili nečijem citatu, ali to vidi u vlastitom okruženju: *„Kad sam ja dobro, mislim da je svima dobro.“*

Kao potvrdu navodi riječi supruge **Mirjane** s nedavnog putovanja s prijateljima u Italiju. Dok su se vozili, rekla mu je: *„Stvarno se isplati moliti za tvoje blagoslove, jer Marko, kad tebi dobro ide, onda svi imamo koristi od toga okolo.“*

Zato smatra da lider mora stalno ulagati u sebe, učiti se i razvijati te ne smije ostati na istoj razini. Od toga koristi imaju tim, ljudi koje vodi, kojima služi i s kojima surađuje. Isto vrijedi za muškarce općenito. Po Markovu mišljenju najgore je kad netko kaže: *„Ja sam takav i to je to, nemam ja prostora za napredak.“* Za muškarca kao glavu obitelji i autoritet to je posebno važno.

Krunoslav tu ubacuje ogradu da je riječ o **duhovnom autoritetu**, „da se ne bi napalili ljevičari“. Marko se nadovezuje šalom da već ima „traume od izvlačenja rečenica na javnim televizijama“. Potvrđuje da misli na duhovni autoritet, odnosno na lidera u vlastitoj obitelji.
sections.subtitle_en: When the Leader Is Well, Everyone Wins
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko quotes a sentence from the GLS about how everyone benefits from the leader being in a good state
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav moves on to a topic that runs through the association's projects: **a man's leadership**. He recalls that they often met at the GLSes and that Marko regularly speaks about it at conferences. He asks him why it is important today for a man to step up as a leader.

Marko responds with a sentence he heard at the GLS: *“When the leader is well, everyone wins.”* He does not know whether it is a slogan or someone's quote, but he sees it in his own environment: *“When I am well, I think everyone is well.”*

As confirmation, he cites the words of his wife **Mirjana** from a recent trip with friends to Italy. While they were driving, she told him: *“It really pays off to pray for your blessings, because Marko, when things are going well for you, then all of us around benefit from it.”*

That is why he believes that a leader must constantly invest in himself, learn, and develop, and must not remain at the same level. The team, the people he leads, whom he serves, and with whom he collaborates benefit from that. The same applies to men in general. In Marko's opinion, the worst is when someone says: *“I am like that and that's it, I have no room for improvement.”* For a man as the head of the family and an authority, this is especially important.

Here, Krunoslav inserts a caveat that this refers to **spiritual authority**, “so that leftists wouldn't get riled up.” Marko follows up with a joke that he already has “trauma from sentences being taken out of context on public television.” He confirms that he means spiritual authority, that is, being the leader in one's own family.

sections.subtitle: Lekcija od sina Jošue: djeca upijaju ono što jesmo
sections.screenshot_description: Marko opisuje trenutak kad je sin Jošua ponovio njegovu lošu naviku
sections.content:
Stalni rad na sebi Marko opravdava jednostavnom logikom: *„Sve što mi jesmo, ćemo prenositi dalje.“* Pitanje je samo što želimo prenijeti. Kaže da na njegov razvoj najviše utječu njegovi sinovi.

Opisuje situaciju koja ga je, kako kaže, „baš prepala“. Sin **Jošua** ponovio je nešto za njim, a radilo se o navici koju Marko nikako nije želio prenijeti. Tada je shvatio da sin upija ono što u njemu vidi. Zaključio je da se mora zapitati što želi da dijete upije i da mora mijenjati sebe i vlastite obrasce ponašanja kako bi sin preuzeo dobar obrazac.

*„Oni će upiti ono što ja jesam. I meni je to dovoljna motivacija da ne prestajem raditi na sebi, da otkrivam sebe, svoje obrasce i da ih mijenjam i da, kako ono kažu popularno, budem najbolja verzija sebe.“*

Krunoslav to sažima ovako: djeca, kao i drugi ljudi, ne preuzimaju ono što im govorimo da bi trebali biti, nego ono što zapravo jesmo. Slijede naš primjer i oponašaju nas.
sections.subtitle_en: A lesson from his son Jošua: children absorb what we are
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko describes the moment when his son Jošua repeated his bad habit
sections.content_en:
Marko justifies constant self-work with simple logic: *"Everything that we are, we will pass on."* The only question is what we want to pass on. He says that his sons have the greatest influence on his development.

He describes a situation that, as he says, "really scared" him. His son **Jošua** repeated something after him, and it was a habit that Marko did not want to pass on at all. It was then that he realized that his son absorbs what he sees in him. He concluded that he must ask himself what he wants the child to absorb and that he must change himself and his own behavior patterns so that his son would adopt a good pattern.

*"They will absorb what I am. And for me, that is enough motivation to not stop working on myself, to discover myself, my patterns and to change them and to, as they popularly say, be the best version of myself."*

Krunoslav summarizes it like this: children, just like other people, do not take on what we tell them they should be, but what we actually are. They follow our example and imitate us.

sections.subtitle: Zašto muškarci više ne zovu djevojke na kavu
sections.screenshot_description: Marko govori o strahu od odbacivanja kao temeljnom strahu muškarca
sections.content:
Krunoslav postavlja aktualno pitanje: zašto su muškarci sve suzdržaniji, sve rjeđe zovu djevojke na kavu i nedostaje im liderske komponente u tom dijelu života? Zašto se boje pristupiti djevojci?

Marko korijen problema vidi u **strahu od odbijanja i odbacivanja**, koji je, kaže, temeljan „pogotovo kod nas muškaraca“. Neuspjeh u pokušaju za muškarca je *„dosta duboko poniženje“*. Ljudi na to reagiraju različito. Neki ostanu uporni i ne odustaju, a drugi se zatvore i upadnu u pasivnost: *„Pokušao sam, nije uspjelo i neću ništa napraviti po tom pitanju.“* Prema njegovu mišljenju, isti obrazac vrijedi i u mnogim drugim područjima života.

Drugi problem je **izbjegavanje odgovornosti**. Marko naglašava da to nije samo muški problem, nego problem društva, i da je kod nas posebno izražen, i u obitelji i u ovakvim situacijama. Odgovornost znači nositi se s posljedicama, znati ih iskanalizirati i riješiti te pogledati sebe. To se potom pretvara u borbu s identitetom i s onim kako se osjećamo nakon neuspjeha. Spominje i predavanje koje je nedavno slušao, u kojem je govornik upravo strah od odbacivanja naveo kao razlog zbog kojeg se muškarci ne upuštaju u nova osvajanja i pothvate.

Krunoslav dodaje da muškarci nakon odbijanja često odu u jedan od dva ekstrema: ili se potpuno zatvore ili pokušavaju osvojiti svaku djevojku pošto-poto. Zlatne sredine, primjećuje, nema.
sections.subtitle_en: Why men no longer ask girls out for coffee
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko speaks about the fear of rejection as a man's fundamental fear
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav raises a topical question: why are men increasingly reserved, asking girls out for coffee less and less often, and lacking a leadership component in that part of life? Why are they afraid to approach a girl?

Marko sees the root of the problem in the **fear of refusal and rejection**, which, he says, is fundamental "especially among us men". Failure in an attempt is *"quite a deep humiliation"* for a man. People react to this differently. Some remain persistent and do not give up, while others close themselves off and fall into passivity: *"I tried, it didn't work, and I won't do anything about it."* In his opinion, the same pattern applies in many other areas of life as well.

The second problem is the **avoidance of responsibility**. Marko emphasizes that this is not only a men's problem, but a societal problem, and that it is particularly pronounced among us, both in the family and in situations like this. Responsibility means dealing with the consequences, knowing how to channel and resolve them, and looking at oneself. This then turns into a struggle with identity and with how we feel after failure. He also mentions a lecture he recently listened to, in which the speaker cited precisely the fear of rejection as the reason why men do not venture into new conquests and endeavors.

Krunoslav adds that after rejection, men often go to one of two extremes: they either close themselves off completely or try to conquer every girl at all costs. There is no golden mean, he notes.

sections.subtitle: Pet godina upornosti: kako je Marko osvojio Mirjanu
sections.screenshot_description: Marko otkriva da je dan snimanja upravo osma godišnjica njegova braka
sections.content:
Krunoslav zamoli gosta da podijeli „mini svjedočanstvo“ o tome kako je godinama osvajao suprugu **Mirjanu**. Marko u šali kaže da ga odbijanja „nisu baš potresla“. Ozbiljnije objašnjava da je uporan i u drugim područjima: prepreka za njega nije kraj priče, nego povod da smisli kako doći do cilja, makar sve trenutno govorilo da ne može. Osvajanje je trajalo oko **pet godina**.

Tijekom razgovora otkriva da je dan snimanja upravo **osma godišnjica braka**. Krunoslav se našali da je baš taj dan odlučio doći na podcast, a Marko dodaje da ga je supruga taman pitala kad misli doći doma.

Ograđuje se da to nije savjet za sve. Netko s trideset godina neće sljedećih pet ili šest godina čekati da se druga osoba odluči. Marko je tada imao 19 godina i nije mu se žurilo. Upravo je izašao iz duge veze, pa je bio, kako kaže, „na prisilnom samovanju“, što danas smatra dobrim za sebe.

Mirjana mu je stalno govorila da ima skrivene namjere. On joj je odgovarao da ništa ne skriva jer joj je rekao sve: sve što radi, radi jer je osvaja. Ona se ipak nije mogla opustiti ni razviti povjerenje. Marko je pokušavao svakih nekoliko mjeseci, *„A sad? A sad? A sad?“*, sve dok **nakon četiri godine** nije potpuno odustao. Tek tada je u njoj „nešto proradilo“.

Mirjana je imala **dva sna** u kojima joj je, kako Marko prenosi, Bog jasno pokazao da je on taj za kojeg se treba odlučiti. Istodobno joj je poručeno da mu ništa ne smije reći i da ga mora pustiti na miru dok se sam ne predomisli. Marko je u to vrijeme ušao u vezu, kako kaže, „uletio“ u nju jer je htio krenuti dalje, ali u njoj nije vidio budućnost i prekinuo ju je. Mirjana mu ni tada ništa nije govorila. Nakon nekoliko mjeseci Marko je odlučio pokušati još jednom i tada je, **2015. godine**, krenulo.

I to je imalo zaplet. Mirjana je rekla „da, može“, a zatim „a nisam sigurna“. Marko smatra da mu je Bog dao milost da u tom trenutku dobro reagira: *„Ma nema veze, uzmi si vremena, pričekat ćemo.“* Od tada su zajedno, deset godina, od čega osam u braku.
sections.subtitle_en: Five years of persistence: how Marko won over Mirjana
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko reveals that the day of recording is precisely his eighth wedding anniversary
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav asks the guest to share a “mini-testimony” about how he spent years winning over his wife **Mirjana**. Marko jokingly says that the rejections “didn't really shake” him. More seriously, he explains that he is persistent in other areas as well: an obstacle for him is not the end of the story, but a reason to figure out how to reach the goal, even if everything currently suggests that he cannot. Winning her over lasted about **five years**.

During the conversation, he reveals that the day of recording is precisely the **eighth wedding anniversary**. Krunoslav jokes that he decided to come to the podcast on that very day, and Marko adds that his wife had just asked him when he planned to come home.

He qualifies that this is not advice for everyone. Someone who is thirty years old will not wait the next five or six years for the other person to make up their mind. Marko was 19 years old at the time and was in no rush. He had just come out of a long relationship, so he was, as he says, “in forced solitude,” which he considers good for himself today.

Mirjana kept telling him that he had hidden intentions. He would reply to her that he was hiding nothing because he had told her everything: everything he does, he does because he is winning her over. Still, she could not relax or develop trust. Marko kept trying every few months, *“And now? And now? And now?”*, until, **after four years**, he gave up completely. Only then did “something click” inside her.

Mirjana had **two dreams** in which, as Marko conveys, God clearly showed her that he was the one she should choose. At the same time, she was told that she must not tell him anything and that she had to leave him alone until he changed his mind on his own. Marko entered a relationship during that time, as he says, “jumped” into it because he wanted to move on, but he saw no future in it and ended it. Mirjana did not say anything to him even then. After a few months, Marko decided to try once more, and that was when, **in 2015**, things started.

And that had a twist as well. Mirjana said “yes, okay,” and then “well, I'm not sure.” Marko considers that God gave him the grace to react well in that moment: *“Never mind, take your time, we'll wait.”* Since then, they have been together, ten years, eight of which in marriage.

sections.subtitle: Mirjanin strah od nesigurnog života ovisnog o donacijama
sections.screenshot_description: Marko objašnjava čega se Mirjana bojala kad je ulazila u vezu s njim
sections.content:
Krunoslav primjećuje da su nakon početka veze brzo uslijedile zaruke i vjenčanje. Marko potvrđuje da su oboje bili svjesni da veza vodi prema braku. Upravo toga se Mirjana bojala.

Marko je već tada pokazivao u kojem će smjeru ići njegov život i da će biti posvećen onome čemu je i danas posvećen. Mirjana je, kaže, htjela *„sve samo ne takvu nesigurnost“*. Željela je miran i siguran život, a Markov put značio je ovisnost o **donacijama i podršci**, uz osjećaj da „sve visi nad glavom“.

Nesigurnost je imala i svoj godišnji ritam. Dvije do tri godine zaredom, u isto doba godine, pred rujan, trajala bi dva do tri mjeseca strepnje: *„Ide dalje, ne ide dalje, šta ću onda, kako će biti?“* Krunoslav dobacuje da mu je ta priča jako poznata.
sections.subtitle_en: Mirjana's fear of an insecure life dependent on donations
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko explains what Mirjana was afraid of when she entered into a relationship with him
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav observes that after the start of the relationship, engagement and marriage quickly followed. Marko confirms that both were aware that the relationship was leading toward marriage. That was precisely what Mirjana was afraid of.

Marko was already showing back then in which direction his life would go and that he would be devoted to what he is devoted to today as well. Mirjana, he says, wanted *„anything but such insecurity“*. She wanted a peaceful and secure life, and Marko's path meant dependence on **donations and support**, with the feeling that „everything hangs over one's head“.

The insecurity also had its annual rhythm. For two to three years in a row, at the same time of year, before September, two to three months of anxiety would last: *„It goes on, it doesn't go on, what will I do then, how will it be?“* Krunoslav chimes in that that story is very familiar to him.

sections.subtitle: Korona, depresija i supruga koja je vjerovala
sections.screenshot_description: Marko se prisjeća krize za vrijeme korone i Mirjanine podrške
sections.content:
Kad je jednom prihvatila takav život, Mirjana mu je postala velika podrška. Marko to najbolje vidi na primjeru razdoblja **korone**, o kojem su razgovarali i na dan snimanja.

Tada je, priznaje, bio **u depresiji**, a da toga nije ni bio svjestan. Sve se zaustavilo. Udruga se bavi edukacijama i nastupima pred ljudima, a odjednom ništa nije funkcioniralo. Otvarala su se pitanja hoće li donatori nastaviti davati i hoće li se udruga morati ugasiti. Istodobno je stao i Mirjanin posao, edukacija javnog nastupa, koja se također odvija uživo.

Mirjana mu je tada rekla nešto čega su se nedavno ponovno prisjetili: *„Ja sam vjerovala da ćeš ti to izvući na kraju i da će biti dobro.“* Tako je i bilo. Od **2020. do 2022.** sve je krenulo uzlazno i stabiliziralo se. Marko kaže da ni danas ništa nije posve sigurno, ali je stanje „onako sigurno“.

Zaključuje s dozom ironije da je Mirjana predosjetila da bi tako moglo biti i htjela je to izbjeći, ali je na kraju ipak „završila u tome“ s njim. Krunoslav dodaje: *„Predosjete žene mnogo toga.“*
sections.subtitle_en: Corona, depression and a wife who believed
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko recalls the crisis during corona and Mirjana's support
sections.content_en:
Once she accepted such a life, Mirjana became a great support to him. Marko sees this best in the example of the period of **corona**, which they also discussed on the day of the recording.

At that time, he admits, he was **in depression**, without even being aware of it. Everything stopped. The association deals with education and appearances before people, and suddenly nothing worked. Questions arose as to whether donors would continue to give and whether the association would have to shut down. At the same time, Mirjana's work also stopped, public speaking training, which also takes place live.

Mirjana then told him something they recently recalled again: *„I believed that you would pull this off in the end and that it would be good.“* And so it was. From **2020 to 2022**, everything moved upward and stabilized. Marko says that even today nothing is completely certain, but the situation is „kind of certain“.

He concludes with a dose of irony that Mirjana sensed that it could be like that and wanted to avoid it, but in the end she nevertheless „ended up in it“ with him. Krunoslav adds: *„Women sense many things.“*

sections.subtitle: Dva poduzetnika, dvoje djece i život u kontra smjenama
sections.screenshot_description: Marko opisuje razdoblje kad su se supružnici izmjenjivali u brizi za djecu
sections.content:
Krunoslav pita kako danas izgleda njihova svakodnevica kad su oboje lideri, on u udruzi, a ona u vlastitom poslu, uz djecu i, kako kaže, apostolate.

Marko odgovara jednom riječju: **„Teško.“** Zahtjevno je jer su oboje poduzetnici. Kao čelnik udruge ne zna unaprijed odakle će doći novac i ne odrađuje samo svoj posao, nego mora smisliti i financiranje. Isto vrijedi za Mirjanu, koja ima **vlastitu firmu za edukacije**. Po struci je **profesorica hrvatskog jezika i retorike**. Marko ju je potaknuo da ne ide raditi u školu, nego da pokrene vlastiti posao, jer je u tome, kaže, „vrhunska“.

Najteže je bilo nakon rođenja sinova, najprije **Jošue**, a zatim i drugog sina, **Jana**. Postoji razdoblje od osam do devet mjeseci u kojem Mirjana ponovno počinje raditi, Marko radi, a dijete još ne ide u vrtić. Tada su radili u kontra smjenama: *„Nekad bude šest dana, mi smo samo spavali doma u krevetu u isto vrijeme.“* Netko je uvijek morao biti s djecom, a stalnu pomoć u čuvanju nemaju, osim kod većih prilika.

Marko iskreno priznaje da nisu uvijek imali razumijevanja jedno za drugo. U tim intenzivnim razdobljima „pucaju po šavovima“, a to se odražava na odnos jer se ne viđaju, ne komuniciraju i nemaju zajedničkog vremena. Ključ opstanka vidi u **međusobnom razumijevanju, podršci i jasnom dogovoru**: *„Gle, to je sad takvo vrijeme, ti trebaš svoje stiskati, ja imam svoje.“* U takvim razdobljima vide se tek nedjeljom, kad su svi zajedno.

Zbog edukacija, putovanja i duhovnih obnova Marko je jedno vrijeme morao ograničiti izbivanja na **dva puta mjesečno** i doslovno odbijati sve ostale pozive kako bi sačuvao vrijeme s obitelji. *„Zahtjevno je, ali je moguće“*, zaključuje, dok god se razumiju, podržavaju i oboje prihvaćaju takav stil života. Ipak dodaje: *„Izazovno je, borbeno.“*
sections.subtitle_en: Two entrepreneurs, two children, and life on opposite shifts
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko describes the period when the spouses took turns caring for the children
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav asks what their everyday life looks like today when both are leaders, he in an association, and she in her own business, along with children and, as he says, apostolates.

Marko answers in one word: **“Difficult.”** It is demanding because both are entrepreneurs. As the head of an association, he does not know in advance where the money will come from and does not merely do his job, but also has to figure out the financing. The same applies to Mirjana, who has **her own educational training company**. By profession, she is a **professor of Croatian language and rhetoric**. Marko encouraged her not to go work in a school, but to start her own business, because in that, he says, she is “superb.”

The hardest part was after the birth of their sons, first **Jošua**, and then their second son, **Jan**. There is a period of eight to nine months in which Mirjana starts working again, Marko works, and the child does not yet go to kindergarten. At that time, they worked on opposite shifts: *“Sometimes it would be six days, we only slept at home in bed at the same time.”* Someone always had to be with the children, and they do not have constant babysitting help, except on major occasions.

Marko honestly admits that they did not always have understanding for one another. In those intense periods they “burst at the seams,” and this is reflected in the relationship because they do not see each other, do not communicate, and have no time together. He sees the key to survival in **mutual understanding, support, and clear agreement**: *“Look, this is such a time now, you need to push through your things, I have mine.”* In such periods, they only see each other on Sundays, when everyone is together.

Due to educational trainings, travels, and spiritual renewals, Marko had to limit his absences for a time to **twice a month** and literally decline all other invitations in order to preserve time with his family. *“It is demanding, but it is possible,”* he concludes, as long as they understand each other, support each other, and both accept such a lifestyle. Still, he adds: *“It is challenging, combative.”*

sections.subtitle: Brak otključava razine kao u videoigri
sections.screenshot_description: Marko slikovito objašnjava kako brak i djeca otključavaju skrivene obrasce ponašanja
sections.content:
Krunoslav pita je li ga osobno iskustvo potaknulo da se bavi partnerskim odnosima i gdje se u njima „najviše lome koplja“. Marko kaže da mu je to od početka bila draga tema jer uvijek izaziva reakciju: ljudi se ili slažu ili ne slažu, ali to žele čuti. Ipak priznaje da mu je današnje iskustvo potpuno drugačije nego na početku, jer svaka životna faza budi stvari kojih čovjek prije nije bio svjestan.

Prvi problem vidi u tome što **u Hrvatskoj nemamo dobru pripremu za brak**. Najbliže dubljem razgovoru je, prema njegovu mišljenju, zaručnički vikend Zajednice bračnih susreta. Za neke se stvari može pripremiti unaprijed, ali mnoge se otključaju tek u braku.

Kao banalan, ali slikovit primjer navodi dogovor o krpi za pod. U njegovoj obitelji čistilo se krpom, a u Mirjaninoj džogerom. Dogovorili su se za džoger. Poanta je u tome da dvije osobe iz dviju različitih obitelji odjednom stalno žive zajedno. Svatko donosi svoje navike i vlastitu sliku braka, uglavnom upijenu od roditelja.

Marko taj proces opisuje usporedbom iz videoigara: *„Otključao se kao razina na igrici, odjednom si dobio novo oružje.“* Ulaskom u brak otvaraju se obrasci ponašanja i uvjerenja kojih čovjek nije bio svjestan, a s djecom se otvara još jedan sloj.

Navodi osobni primjer. Postojala je stvar koju nije volio kod svog oca i koja ga je živcirala. U jednoj situaciji s Jošuom napravio je potpuno isto. *„Ne mogu vjerovati da sam napravio isto to. A zašto? Zato što sam to gledao.“* Iako mu se to ponašanje nije sviđalo, upio ga je, a dijete ga je „triggeriralo“.

Zaključuje da svaka faza donosi nove izazove i da je ključno imati znanje i alate kojima se može otkriti što se događa, odakle to dolazi i što treba mijenjati.
sections.subtitle_en: Marriage unlocks levels like in a video game
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko vividly explains how marriage and children unlock hidden patterns of behavior
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav asks whether personal experience prompted him to deal with partner relationships and where "spears are broken the most" in them. Marko says that from the beginning this was a dear topic to him because it always provokes a reaction: people either agree or disagree, but they want to hear it. Still, he admits that his experience today is completely different than at the beginning, because every life stage awakens things a person was not aware of before.

He sees the first problem in the fact that **in Croatia we do not have good preparation for marriage**. The closest thing to a deeper conversation is, according to his opinion, the betrothal weekend of the Zajednica bračnih susreta. For some things one can prepare in advance, but many are unlocked only in marriage.

As a banal, but vivid example, he mentions the agreement about the floor cloth. In his family, they cleaned with a cloth, and in Mirjana's with a mop. They agreed on the mop. The point is that two people from two different families are suddenly constantly living together. Everyone brings their own habits and their own picture of marriage, mostly absorbed from parents.

Marko describes that process with a comparison from video games: *“It unlocked like a level in a game, suddenly you got a new weapon.”* By entering marriage, patterns of behavior and beliefs a person was not aware of are opened up, and with children another layer opens up.

He gives a personal example. There was a thing he did not like about his father and that annoyed him. In one situation with Jošua he did completely the same thing. *“I cannot believe that I did the same thing. And why? Because I watched that.”* Even though he did not like that behavior, he absorbed it, and the child "triggered" it.

He concludes that every stage brings new challenges and that it is crucial to have knowledge and tools with which one can discover what is happening, where it comes from, and what needs to be changed.

sections.subtitle: Iza fasade savršene katoličke obitelji
sections.screenshot_description: Marko otvoreno govori o vlastitim problemima i odlasku na psihoterapiju
sections.content:
Marko o braku rado govori jer je, kako ističe, **brak u Hrvatskoj u krizi**. Odlazak u crkvu ne znači nužno dobar brak, a o tome se šuti. Ljudi čuvaju *„sliku idealne katoličke obitelji“* u kojoj su svi sretni, a zapravo ne razgovaraju, udaljeni su, hladni ili „totalno u drugim filmovima“. Boje se priznati probleme pred drugim „savršenim“ katoličkim obiteljima.

Marko sam ide u suprotnom smjeru. U programima otvoreno govori o svojim padovima i greškama. Kad je krenuo na **psihoterapiju**, morao je nagovoriti terapeuta, kojeg osobno poznaje, da ga primi. Na pitanje hoće li mu smetati što će se otkriti neke stvari o njemu odgovorio je: *„80 posto stvari sam izrekao u nekom programu negdje. Ako ti iščupaš ovih 20, molim te, izvuci ih van.“*

Spominje i podcast o seksu nakon kojeg su dobili „more uvreda“, između ostalog i zbog same riječi. Upravo zato smatra važnim o takvim temama govoriti iskreno, kako bi ljudi imali mjesto gdje mogu priznati da i sami imaju problema. Kad je nedavno pred nekoliko prijatelja otvoreno iznio vlastiti problem i slomljenost, bili su šokirani. Jedan mu je rekao: *„Puno sam se toga pronašao, ali nisam mogao to iskomunicirati i reći.“*

*„Mi se možemo praviti super divni, krasni molitveni timovi. Što se to događa iza zatvorenih vrata? To mene zanima“*, kaže Marko. Služba i pomazanje su važni, ali jednako je važna autentičnost privatnog života. Kad privatno nešto ne štima, on se, priznaje, osjeća „kao najveći licemjer“. Poruka je ipak jasna: *„Okej je da nije sve okej.“* I u njihovu su braku bila razdoblja kad su, kako kaže, bili „katastrofa“ i morali se izboriti i isplivati. *„Evo sad se ispovijedam“*, dodaje. Krunoslav se nadovezuje: *„Taman na godišnjicu braka.“*
sections.subtitle_en: Behind the facade of a perfect Catholic family
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko speaks openly about his own problems and going to psychotherapy
sections.content_en:
Marko gladly speaks about marriage because, as he points out, **marriage in Croatia is in crisis**. Going to church does not necessarily mean a good marriage, and people are silent about that. People preserve the *“image of an ideal Catholic family”* in which everyone is happy, but in reality they do not talk, they are distant, cold, or “totally in other movies”. They are afraid to admit problems in front of other “perfect” Catholic families.

Marko himself goes in the opposite direction. In programs he speaks openly about his falls and mistakes. When he started **psychotherapy**, he had to persuade the therapist, whom he knows personally, to take him in. To the question of whether it would bother him that some things about him would be revealed, he replied: *“I have said 80 percent of things in some program somewhere. If you tear out these 20, please, pull them out.”*

He also mentions a podcast about sex after which they received a “sea of insults”, among other things because of the word itself. That is precisely why he considers it important to speak honestly about such topics, so that people would have a place where they can admit that they themselves have problems. When he recently openly presented his own problem and brokenness before a few friends, they were shocked. One told him: *“I found myself in a lot of that, but I could not communicate that and say it.”*

*“We can pretend to be super wonderful, great prayer teams. What is happening behind closed doors? That is what interests me”*, Marko says. Ministry and anointing are important, but the authenticity of private life is equally important. When something is not right privately, he, he admits, feels “like the biggest hypocrite”. The message is nevertheless clear: *“It is okay that not everything is okay.”* And in their marriage there were periods when, as he says, they were a “disaster” and had to fight through and surface. *“Here, now I am confessing”*, he adds. Krunoslav chimes in: *“Just in time for the wedding anniversary.”*

sections.subtitle: Tajni računi i financijski stres koji snižava inteligenciju
sections.screenshot_description: Marko iznosi rezultate istraživanja o parovima sa zajedničkim i razdvojenim financijama
sections.content:
Prelazeći na financije, Krunoslav pita oko čega se bračni parovi najviše „kolju“. Marko odgovara: **oko tajnosti**, odnosno kad supružnici nisu upoznati s financijama jedno drugoga.

Pozivajući se na istraživanja na koja je naišao pripremajući predavanje za nedavnu konferenciju, navodi da **financijski stres doslovno smanjuje kvocijent inteligencije**, točnije radnu memoriju za razmišljanje. Zbog toga donosimo lošije odluke, a to se prelijeva na odnos kroz povlačenje, šutnju, netrpeljivost i ljutnju. Posebno opterećuje dugoročan dug, kad se ne radi o iznosu koji će se vratiti sljedeći mjesec.

Opisuje i istraživanje na, kako se prisjeća, **230 parova** prosječne dobi oko 28 godina na početku braka:

- trećina je imala **zajedničke financije**;
- trećina je bila **upoznata s financijama** jedno drugoga;
- trećina je imala **razdvojene financije**.

Nakon dvije godine ponovljen je test zadovoljstva. Parovi sa zajedničkim financijama imali su najbolje rezultate, *„daleko puno bolje“* od onih s razdvojenim financijama.

Razdvojene financije, prema Marku, ostavljaju mnogo prostora za skrivanje i „padanje u grijeh“: kocku, nepotrebno trošenje, stvaranje dugova i loše upravljanje novcem. Kad još netko vidi stanje, postoji određena kontrola. Ne radi se o nadgledniku, nego o tome da *„barem još netko vidi“*.

Posebno upozorava na **kockanje**. Poznaje nekoliko bliskih slučajeva muškaraca koji su upali u ogromne dugove i uništili obitelji. *„To nisu ljudi koji su tamo daleki ovisnici. To su ljudi u crkvi svaki dan.“* Prokockali su, kaže, more novca, automobile i stanove.
sections.subtitle_en: Secret accounts and financial stress that lowers intelligence
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko presents research results about couples with joint and separate finances
sections.content_en:
Moving on to finances, Krunoslav asks what married couples “slaughter each other” over the most. Marko answers: **over secrecy**, that is, when spouses are not familiar with each other's finances.

Referring to research he came across while preparing a lecture for a recent conference, he states that **financial stress literally reduces intelligence quotient**, more precisely the working memory for thinking. Because of this we make worse decisions, and that spills over into the relationship through withdrawal, silence, intolerance, and anger. Long-term debt is especially burdensome, when it is not about an amount that will be repaid next month.

He also describes research on, as he recalls, **230 couples** with an average age of about 28 years at the beginning of marriage:

- a third had **joint finances**;
- a third was **familiar with each other's finances**;
- a third had **separate finances**.

After two years, the satisfaction test was repeated. Couples with joint finances had the best results, *“far much better”* than those with separate finances.

Separate finances, according to Marko, leave a lot of room for hiding and “falling into sin”: gambling, unnecessary spending, creating debts, and poor money management. When someone else sees the state, a certain control exists. It is not about an overseer, but about the fact that *“at least someone else sees”*.

He especially warns against **gambling**. He knows several close cases of men who fell into huge debts and destroyed families. *“Those are not people who are distant addicts over there. Those are people in church every day.”* They gambled away, he says, a sea of money, cars, and apartments.

sections.subtitle: Granica od 20 eura i glas razuma za nove tenisice
sections.screenshot_description: Marko objašnjava kako on i Mirjana dogovaraju trošenje novca
sections.content:
Marko otkriva kako to funkcionira kod njih. Nemaju zajednički račun, ali imaju dogovoreni iznos, otprilike **do 20 eura**, za koji ne moraju pitati drugoga. Sve iznad toga moraju reći. Ne radi se o traženju odobrenja, nego o informiranju: *„E, znaš šta, treba mi to, kupit ću nešto.“*

Za neke kupnje treba mu i savjet, priznaje uz smijeh: *„Ja bih rado potrošio na još jedne tenisice i treba mi neki glas razuma koji će mi reći: E, Marko, mislim da je to pretjerivanje.“* Isto vrijedi i u obrnutom smjeru.
sections.subtitle_en: A 20-euro limit and a voice of reason for new sneakers
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko explains how he and Mirjana agree on spending money
sections.content_en:
Marko reveals how it works with them. They do not have a joint account, but they have an agreed-upon amount, roughly **up to 20 euros**, for which they do not have to ask the other. Everything above that they have to tell. It is not about asking for approval, but about informing: *„Hey, you know what, I need that, I'm going to buy something.“*

For some purchases he also needs advice, he admits with a laugh: *„I would gladly spend on another pair of sneakers and I need some voice of reason that will tell me: Hey, Marko, I think that's an exaggeration.“* The same applies in the reverse direction.

sections.subtitle: Kartice i rate nasuprot gotovini: kako je Mirjana promijenila Markov pogled na novac
sections.screenshot_description: Marko uspoređuje financijske navike svoje i Mirjanine obitelji
sections.content:
Marko priznaje da mu se pogled na financije uz Mirjanu **drastično promijenio**. Došao je iz obitelji u kojoj su se koristile kartice, krediti i rate. Mirjana dolazi iz obitelji u kojoj vrijedi pravilo: *ako nemamo dovoljno novca odmah, ne kupujemo*. Karticu na rate ima, ali, kako kaže Marko, ni ne zna gdje joj je. Kod nje je samo „cash and carry“.

Morali su naći sredinu. Kad su podizali kredit, Marko joj je morao objasniti: *„Mirjana, nećemo ga otplatiti za pet godina.“* Kredit se ne može riješiti preko noći. Može se štedjeti, odvajati sa strane i zatvarati dio po dio, ali Mirjanin strah od takvog opterećenja bio je velik i trebalo ga je dovesti „u neku normalu“.

Zahvaljujući njezinim navikama Marko je, kaže, svoj odnos prema novcu bitno popravio. Danas misli da je stvar „više-manje u kontroli“. Upravlja novcem mudrije, bez odlaska u krajnosti, s jasnom idejom gdje ulagati, što davati i kako trošiti. Supružnici su danas, zaključuje, „na istoj valnoj duljini“.
sections.subtitle_en: Cards and installments versus cash: how Mirjana changed Marko's view of money
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko compares the financial habits of his and Mirjana's family
sections.content_en:
Marko admits that his view of finances **drastically changed** with Mirjana. He came from a family where cards, loans, and installments were used. Mirjana comes from a family where the rule is: *if we don't have enough money immediately, we don't buy*. She has an installment card, but, as Marko says, she doesn't even know where it is. With her, it is only „cash and carry“.

They had to find a middle ground. When they were taking out a loan, Marko had to explain to her: *„Mirjana, we will not pay it off in five years.“* A loan cannot be resolved overnight. One can save, set aside, and close piece by piece, but Mirjana's fear of such a burden was great and it needed to be brought „to some normality“.

Thanks to her habits, Marko says, he significantly improved his relationship with money. Today he thinks that the matter is „more or less under control“. He manages money more wisely, without going to extremes, with a clear idea of where to invest, what to give, and how to spend. The spouses are today, he concludes, „on the same wavelength“.

sections.subtitle: Neka novcem upravlja sposobniji i nije sramota tražiti pomoć
sections.screenshot_description: Marko poručuje da novcem treba upravljati sposobniji partner, bez obzira na to je li to muž
sections.content:
Ovdje Marko ponavlja misao iz uvodnog isječka. Kad jedan partner ne zna upravljati novcem, neka to prepusti onome tko zna. Uobičajeno je mišljenje da je muškarac lider i glava, ali *„ima muškaraca koji ne znaju upravljati novcima, a ako je žena sposobnija, daj njoj da ona upravlja novcima“*. Ako muž uporno troši i srlja, rješenje nije da žena pasivno kaže *„on je glava, neka on odluči“*, nego da preuzme upravljanje. *„Inače ćete biti u problemima.“*

Na nedavnom predavanju o financijama poručio je: ako vam stalno curi, ako ste stalno u minusu i u dugovima i „vrtite iz šupljeg u prazno“, **potražite pomoć**. *„Nije to sramota.“* Savjetuje razgovor s nekim tko će pogledati stanje sa strane i reći što treba srezati i dovesti u red. Sramota je, kaže, bojati se tražiti pomoć, a ne priznati da ne znamo.

Kao primjer navodi poznanika koji upravlja bogatstvom **nogometaša** i drugih bogatih ljudi koji ne znaju što bi s novcem. Imati novac ne znači biti „najpametniji na svijetu“. Isto vrijedi na manjim razinama: može se pitati stručnjaka ili prijatelja koji dobro upravlja novcem. Iz dugova se ne izlazi preko noći, jer se u njima nismo ni našli preko noći, pa treba plan i taktika.

Navodi i otrežnjujući primjer **braka koji se raspao** dok su supružnici bili u dvadesetima, nakon samo nekoliko godina. Jedna osoba nije znala ništa o financijama i dobivala je samo džeparac, a na kraju su se pojavili veliki dugovi i kaos. *„Opasno je područje“*, zaključuje Marko, i savjetuje parovima da razgovaraju i uče o novcu, *„jer se o tome uči“*.
sections.subtitle_en: Let the more capable one manage money and it is no shame to seek help
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko conveys that money should be managed by the more capable partner, regardless of whether that is the husband
sections.content_en:
Here Marko repeats the thought from the introductory clip. When one partner does not know how to manage money, let them leave it to the one who does. The common opinion is that the man is the leader and the head, but *„there are men who do not know how to manage money, and if the woman is more capable, let her manage the money“*. If the husband persistently spends and rushes recklessly, the solution is not for the wife to passively say *„he is the head, let him decide“*, but to take over management. *„Otherwise you will be in trouble.“*

At a recent lecture on finances, he conveyed: if you are constantly leaking, if you are constantly in the red and in debt and „spinning from hollow into empty“, **seek help**. *„That is no shame.“* He advises talking to someone who will look at the situation from the outside and say what needs to be cut and put in order. It is a shame, he says, to be afraid to ask for help, not to admit that we do not know.

As an example, he mentions an acquaintance who manages the wealth of **football players** and other wealthy people who do not know what to do with their money. Having money does not mean being the „smartest in the world“. The same applies at smaller levels: one can ask an expert or a friend who manages money well. One does not get out of debt overnight, because we did not find ourselves in it overnight either, so a plan and tactics are needed.

He also mentions the sobering example of a **marriage that fell apart** while the spouses were in their twenties, after only a few years. One person knew nothing about finances and received only pocket money, and in the end large debts and chaos emerged. *„It is a dangerous area“*, concludes Marko, and advises couples to talk and learn about money, *„because one learns about that“*.

sections.subtitle: Financijski odgoj počinje džeparcem za užinu
sections.screenshot_description: Marko opisuje kako petogodišnjeg sina Jošuu uči raspoređivati novac
sections.content:
Krunoslav predlaže da se parovi financijama bave još prije braka, kroz programe i savjetovanja, jer se na zaručničkim tečajevima ta pitanja tek spomenu. Marko ide korak dalje: dobra priprema ne počinje prije braka, nego već **u osnovnoj školi**. Prvi susret s novcem je džeparac za užinu i tada treba naučiti raspolagati njime.

Opisuje kako to radi sa sinom **Jošuom**, koji ima pet godina. Kad Jošua dobije novac, otac ga uči da ga rasporedi: dio ostavlja za štednju, dio može pokloniti nekome kome treba pomoć, a 10 posto odvaja za **Eho Kids**. Program za djecu je besplatan, ali Marko mu objašnjava: *„Ajde, podrži program, odvoji te novce, to nisu tvoji novci.“* Jošua tako već sada uči koliko što vrijedi, koliko treba skupiti i koliko mu još fali u kasici.

Prepričava i video nekog milijardera koji je sinu davao tjedni džeparac i učio ga da dio štedi, dio donira, a ostatak troši. Kad ga je sin zamolio da mu kupi Coca-Colu, otac mu je rekao da je kupi sam. Kad je dječak vidio da stoji oko dva dolara, odustao je jer mu je bila preskupa. Iako je otac imao milijarde, želio je da sin nauči da raspolaže onim što ima i da ne može uvijek računati na očevu pomoć.
sections.subtitle_en: Financial education begins with pocket money for a snack
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko describes how he teaches his five-year-old son Jošua to allocate money
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav suggests that couples deal with finances even before marriage, through programs and counseling, because at pre-Cana courses these issues are merely mentioned. Marko goes a step further: good preparation does not begin before marriage, but already **in elementary school**. The first encounter with money is pocket money for a snack, and that is when one should learn to manage it.

He describes how he does this with his son **Jošua**, who is five years old. When Jošua gets money, his father teaches him to allocate it: he leaves a portion for savings, he can gift a portion to someone who needs help, and he sets aside 10 percent for **Eho Kids**. The program for children is free, but Marko explains to him: *“Come on, support the program, set aside that money, that is not your money.”* In this way, Jošua is already learning how much something is worth, how much he needs to collect, and how much he is still missing in his piggy bank.

He also recounts a video of a billionaire who gave his son a weekly allowance and taught him to save part, donate part, and spend the rest. When his son asked him to buy him a Coca-Cola, the father told him to buy it himself. When the boy saw that it cost about two dollars, he gave up because it was too expensive for him. Even though the father had billions, he wanted his son to learn to manage what he has and that he cannot always count on his father's help.

sections.subtitle: Razgovor o novcu prije oltara
sections.screenshot_description: Marko prepričava Mirjaninu zabrinutost zbog načina trošenja prije braka
sections.content:
Za one koji takvo znanje nisu stekli u djetinjstvu Marko ima jasan savjet: o novcu treba razgovarati **prije braka**. Kao primjer navodi vlastito iskustvo. Prije vjenčanja bilo je nekoliko situacija u kojima je Mirjana bila zabrinuta kako će se postaviti zbog jedne obiteljske situacije vezane uz trošenje novca.

Rekla mu je: *„Sve pet, mi sad nismo u braku, ali mene brine misliš li ti da je to okej, taj način trošenja? Jer kasnije ćemo mi biti skupa, i ako je tebi ovo okej, onda imamo problem.“* Marko je tada morao jasno razdvojiti vlastite stavove od obiteljskih navika i pratiti kako se postavlja.

Tim primjerom zatvara se blok o financijama u braku. Marko je spomenuo davanje desetine i darivanje, što je Krunoslavu poslužilo kao prijelaz na sljedeće pitanje.
sections.subtitle_en: A conversation about money before the altar
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko recounts Mirjana's concern regarding spending habits before marriage
sections.content_en:
For those who did not acquire such knowledge in childhood, Marko has clear advice: money should be discussed **before marriage**. As an example, he cites his own experience. Before the wedding, there were several situations in which Mirjana was concerned about how he would position himself regarding a family situation related to spending money.

She told him: *"Everything's fine, we are not married now, but it worries me whether you think that is okay, that way of spending? Because later we will be together, and if this is okay with you, then we have a problem."* Marko then had to clearly separate his own attitudes from family habits and monitor how he positioned himself.

That example closes the block on finances in marriage. Marko mentioned tithing and giving, which served Krunoslav as a transition to the next question.
