sections.subtitle: „Iskušajte me”: desetina kao jedino mjesto gdje Bog dopušta da ga se kuša
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Krunoslav citira proroka Malahiju i otvara temu desetine
sections.content:
Drugi dio razgovora otvara pitanje koje se u katoličkim krugovima rijetko postavlja naglas. Voditelj **Krunoslav** primjećuje da se Marko Matijašević u prethodnom odgovoru već dotaknuo desetine, opisujući kako svog sina uči da odvaja 10% za program Echo Kids. Krunoslav zatim pita kakav bi trebao biti stav katolika prema desetini. Upozorava da se vjernici tom temom vrlo malo bave i vrlo malo daruju. Razumije da mnogi imaju financijskih problema, pa se grčevito drže iznosa koji imaju.

Krunoslav dodaje osobnu crtu. Tog je dana naišao na citat iz knjige proroka Malahije, koji slobodno parafrazira: *„Ako želiš iskušati Gospodina, daj desetinu i vidi što će On učiniti.”* Svjedoči da on i supruga izdvajaju desetinu i da im se ona **mnogostruko vraća**. Ponekad to zaborave jer rješavaju druge stvari, ali ipak vide koliko ih Bog blagoslivlja kad daju od onoga što im je povjerio na upravljanje.

Marko Matijašević nadovezuje se na isti tekst i ističe njegovu posebnost. Prema njegovim riječima, desetina je **jedina stvar u Bibliji za koju Bog kaže da ga smijemo kušati**. Vjernici znaju zapovijed *„Ne kušaj Boga svoga”*, a ovdje stoji suprotno: *„Kušajte me, dajte prvine u moju riznicu i onda me iskušajte neću li onda izlit blagoslov na vas.”* Gost otkriva da je i sam tog dana nekome slao baš taj citat. Zaključuje da vjernik na tom području doslovno ima Božje dopuštenje da ga iskuša, pa se pita zašto to ne prihvatiti.
sections.subtitle_en: "Test me": the tithe as the only place where God allows Himself to be tested
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Krunoslav quotes the prophet Malachi and opens the topic of the tithe
sections.content_en:
The second part of the conversation opens a question that is rarely raised out loud in Catholic circles. Host **Krunoslav** notes that Marko Matijašević already touched upon the tithe in his previous answer, describing how he teaches his son to set aside 10% for the Echo Kids program. Krunoslav then asks what a Catholic's attitude toward the tithe should be. He warns that the faithful deal very little with that topic and give very little. He understands that many have financial problems, so they cling tightly to the amounts they have.

Krunoslav adds a personal note. That day, he came across a quote from the Book of the Prophet Malachi, which he freely paraphrases: *"If you want to test the Lord, give a tithe and see what He will do."* He testifies that he and his wife set aside a tithe and that it **returns to them manifold**. Sometimes they forget it because they are dealing with other things, but they still see how much God blesses them when they give from what He has entrusted to them to manage.

Marko Matijašević builds upon the same text and highlights its uniqueness. According to his words, the tithe is **the only thing in the Bible about which God says that we may test Him**. The faithful know the commandment *"Do not test your God"*, and here stands the opposite: *"Test me, bring the firstfruits into my storehouse, and then test me if I will not then pour out a blessing upon you."* The guest reveals that he himself was sending that very quote to someone that day. He concludes that in this area a believer literally has God's permission to test Him, so he wonders why not accept it.

sections.subtitle: Zašto Crkva šuti o novcu i zašto vjersko ne mora biti besplatno
sections.screenshot_description: Marko Matijašević objašnjava zašto se u Crkvi izbjegava tema financija
sections.content:
Marko Matijašević smatra da se o desetini šuti zato što se **u Crkvi općenito slabo govori o financijama**. Ljudi su na tom području već povrijeđeni i uglavnom imaju negativan stav prema toj temi. Zato razumije svećenike koji se ustručavaju o tome govoriti, jer od vjernika često čuju reakciju: *„Nemoj mi još s tim i u crkvi.”*

Iz toga proizlazi problem s kojim se njegova udruga Eho često susreće. Postoji očekivanje da sve što je vjersko mora biti besplatno, kao da ništa ne vrijedi i treba se samo dijeliti. Gost navodi tipičan prigovor: *„Ne mogu vjerovati da naplaćujete čitanje Božje riječi.”* Odgovara da se to ne naplaćuje. Svatko si može kupiti Bibliju i čitati je sam. Ono što se plaća jest sve ostalo:

- **uloženo vrijeme** i trud organizatora,
- **tehnika i oprema**,
- sadržaj koji posjetitelj dobiva „serviran”, a kojem se netko posvetio kroz mnogo sati rada.

Matijašević tvrdi da oni koji vjernicima prešućuju ovu temu iz obzira prema njihovoj povrijeđenosti ne čine im uslugu. Time im, kaže, propuštaju objasniti koji blagoslov donosi davanje i što Bog misli o financijama.
sections.subtitle_en: Why the Church is silent about money and why what is religious does not have to be free
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko Matijašević explains why the topic of finances is avoided in the Church
sections.content_en:
Marko Matijašević believes that there is silence about the tithe because **in the Church in general, little is said about finances**. People are already hurt in that area and mostly have a negative attitude toward that topic. That is why he understands priests who hesitate to speak about it, because they often hear the reaction from the faithful: *„Don't bring that up to me in church too.”*

From this arises the problem that his udruga Eho often encounters. There is an expectation that everything that is religious must be free, as if it is worth nothing and should only be given away. The guest cites a typical objection: *„I cannot believe that you charge for reading the Word of God.”* He replies that this is not what is being charged for. Anyone can buy a Bible and read it themselves. What is paid for is everything else:

- **invested time** and the organizers' effort,
- **technology and equipment**,
- content that the visitor receives „served”, and to which someone dedicated themselves through many hours of work.

Matijašević claims that those who keep silent about this topic before the faithful out of consideration for their hurt do not do them a favor. In doing so, he says, they fail to explain to them what blessing giving brings and what God thinks about finances.

sections.subtitle: Desetina nije milostinja: Tobijinih 30 posto i sedam židovskih davanja
sections.screenshot_description: Gost razlikuje desetinu od milostinje na primjeru Tobije
sections.content:
Jedna od ključnih poanti epizode jest razlika koju vjernici često ne prave. Matijašević kaže da je davanje milostinje ili donacija za humanitarnu svrhu za većinu ljudi normalna stvar. **To, međutim, nije desetina.** Po njegovu tumačenju, desetina je namijenjena isključivo **evangelizaciji i izgradnji hrama**: ide Bogu, onima koji mu služe i širenju vjere. *„Pomoć prijatelju u nevolji nije desetina”*, naglašava.

Kao ilustraciju vraća se Tobiji, kojeg je spomenuo na početku razgovora kad je govorio o temeljima udruge Eho. Prema gostu, Tobija je davao čak **30% svojih primanja**:

- **10%** za hram,
- **10%** kao milostinju,
- **10%** trošio je kod svojih sunarodnjaka, kupujući njihove proizvode i potičući njihovo gospodarstvo.

Matijašević dodaje širi kontekst. Židovi su poznavali oko **sedam vrsta davanja**, uključujući razne žrtve i paljenice, a desetina je bila samo jedna od njih. Danas, kaže, dovoljno je spomenuti samo desetinu pa nastaje *„plač i škrgut zuba”*. Tema je osjetljiva upravo zbog te povrijeđenosti, a o blagoslovu koji ona nosi govori se premalo.
sections.subtitle_en: Tithe is not alms: Tobit's 30 percent and seven Jewish offerings
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest distinguishes the tithe from alms using the example of Tobit
sections.content_en:
One of the key points of the episode is a distinction that believers often do not make. Matijašević says that giving alms or donations for a humanitarian purpose is a normal thing for most people. **That, however, is not a tithe.** According to his interpretation, the tithe is intended exclusively for **evangelization and the building of the temple**: it goes to God, to those who serve him, and to the spreading of the faith. *“Helping a friend in need is not a tithe,”* he emphasizes.

As an illustration, he returns to Tobit, whom he mentioned at the beginning of the conversation when he spoke about the foundations of the association Eho. According to the guest, Tobit gave as much as **30% of his income**:

- **10%** for the temple,
- **10%** as alms,
- **10%** he spent among his compatriots, buying their products and stimulating their economy.

Matijašević adds a broader context. The Jews knew of about **seven types of offerings**, including various sacrifices and burnt offerings, and the tithe was only one of them. Today, he says, it is enough to mention only the tithe, and *“weeping and gnashing of teeth”* arises. The topic is sensitive precisely because of that hurt, and too little is said about the blessing it brings.

sections.subtitle: Novi zavjet ne ukida desetinu: ljubav ide iznad zakona, a ne ispod njega
sections.screenshot_description: Marko Matijašević objašnjava da ljubav nadilazi zakon
sections.content:
Matijašević se zatim osvrće na čest prigovor. Mnogi se pozivaju na Novi zavjet, u kojem Pavao kaže da svatko daje *„kako je srcem odlučio”* jer *„Bog ljubi vesela darivatelja”*. Iz toga zaključuju da desetina više ne vrijedi.

Gost na to odgovara dvama argumentima. Prvo, **Novi zavjet nije ukinuo Stari zavjet**. Drugo, desetina doista jest zakon, ali **ljubav ide iznad zakona**. Ako zakon traži 10%, onda bi ljubav trebala dati više: *„Inače nema ljubavi. Ako ja odrađujem samo ono što moram, to je zakon.”* Odbacuje tumačenje u kojem ljubav znači ukidanje zakona, svedeno na pristup *„sola gratia”* u kojem je sve oprošteno i *„sve divno i krasno”*.

Poziva se i na Pavlove riječi: *„Tko sije oskudno, oskudno će i žeti.”* Ne može se, kaže, sijati oskudno i očekivati blagoslov.

Gost predviđa i sljedeći prigovor: netko ima novca, ne daje desetinu, a ipak izgleda blagoslovljeno. Odgovor mu je jasan: **količina novca na računu ne govori o blagoslovu**. *„Ti možeš imati milijune i biti proklet”*, kaže. Izjednačavanje bogatstva i blagoslova pripisuje teologiji prosperiteta, a ne kršćanskom razumijevanju blagoslova.
sections.subtitle_en: The New Testament does not abolish the tithe: love goes above the law, not below it
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko Matijašević explains that love transcends the law
sections.content_en:
Matijašević then addresses a common objection. Many appeal to the New Testament, in which Paul says that each person gives *“as he decided in his heart”* because *“God loves a cheerful giver”*. From this they conclude that the tithe is no longer valid.

The guest responds to this with two arguments. First, **the New Testament did not abolish the Old Testament**. Second, the tithe indeed is the law, but **love goes above the law**. If the law requires 10%, then love should give more: *“Otherwise there is no love. If I only perform what I must, that is the law.”* He rejects the interpretation in which love means the abolition of the law, reduced to a *“sola gratia”* approach in which everything is forgiven and *“everything is lovely and wonderful”*.

He also refers to Paul's words: *“Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly.”* One cannot, he says, sow sparingly and expect a blessing.

The guest also anticipates the next objection: someone has money, does not give a tithe, and yet looks blessed. His answer is clear: **the amount of money in the account does not speak of blessing**. *“You can have millions and be cursed”*, he says. He attributes equating wealth and blessing to prosperity theology, and not to the Christian understanding of blessing.

sections.subtitle: Udovičin novčić i tri eura koja vrijede koliko tuđih sto
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava prispodobu o udovici koja je dala sve što je imala
sections.content:
Kako bi pokazao što je Bogu doista važno, Matijašević podsjeća na događaj u hramu. Isus pita učenike tko je dao najviše dok bogati ubacuju svoje kese, a jedna žena tek nekoliko novčića. Njegov je odgovor da je dala upravo ona, jer su drugi davali od viška, a ona je dala sve što je imala.

Pouka koju gost izvodi glasi: **iz Božje perspektive nije stvar u iznosu**. Ljudima zato poručuje: *„Pa daj ti tri eura.”* Ako je to nečiji trenutni maksimum, to vrijedi jednako kao nečijih sto. Važno je biti vjeran i povjerovati Bogu.

Matijašević dijeli i osobno iskustvo. Od prvog novca koji je zaradio uvijek je izdvajao desetinu, a svjedočanstva koja iz toga ima opisuje kao **ogromna iskustva Božje providnosti**. Posebno naglašava da o tome ne govori radi vlastite koristi: *„Ja neću biti suđen za tvoj dio, ja ću biti za svoj dio. Ti ćeš biti suđen što si napravio s onime što imaš.”*
sections.subtitle_en: The widow's mite and three euros that are worth as much as someone else's hundred
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the parable of the widow who gave everything she had
sections.content_en:
In order to show what is truly important to God, Matijašević recalls the event in the temple. Jesus asks the disciples who gave the most while the rich are putting in their bags, and one woman only a few coins. His answer is that it was precisely she who gave, because others gave out of their surplus, while she gave everything she had.

The lesson the guest draws is: **from God's perspective, it is not a matter of the amount**. That is why he tells people: *„Well, give three euros then.”* If that is someone's current maximum, it is worth just as much as someone else's hundred. It is important to be faithful and to trust God.

Matijašević also shares a personal experience. From the first money he earned, he always set aside a tithe, and the testimonies he has from this he describes as **enormous experiences of God's providence**. He especially emphasizes that he does not speak about this for his own benefit: *„I will not be judged for your part, I will be for my part. You will be judged for what you did with what you have.”*

sections.subtitle: Samo vjernik daje za evangelizaciju: protestanti, kalež od dijamanta i stare stolice
sections.screenshot_description: Matijašević uspoređuje katolike i protestante te govori o kaležu
sections.content:
Matijašević ističe razliku između humanitarnog davanja i davanja za evangelizaciju. **Za humanitarnu svrhu dat će svatko**, pa i nevjernik kad vidi veliku potrebu. Za evangelizaciju će dati samo vjernik, jer nevjerniku ona ništa ne znači.

U tome vidi i razlog zašto su protestanti na Zapadu, kako kaže, uspješniji od katolika. Za protestante je davanje desetine i ulaganje u evangelizaciju sasvim normalna stvar. Katolici bi, prema njegovim riječima, najradije da sve bude *„štalica”*, pa se odmah pitaju zašto je sve u crkvi tako skupo.

Gost misli drukčije: *„Pa nek budu skupe stvari.”* Kao primjer uzima **kalež**. U njemu je krv Kristova koja je spasila vjernika, pa neka bude i od dijamanta, umjesto obične šalice za koju neki misle da je dovoljna.

Prepričava i anegdotu jednog propovjednika koji je uređivao molitvenu dvoranu. Ljudi su mu nudili stolice koje im kod kuće više ne trebaju, a on je uzvratio pitanjem: *„Te stolice nisu dovoljno dobre za tvoju kuću, a dovoljno su dobre za Božji dom?”* U dvoranu su na kraju stavljene nove stolice. Razlog je, kaže Matijašević, to što **Bog zaslužuje najbolje** i što takav odnos pokazuje koliko je čovjeku stalo.

Na kraju poglavlja poziva se na proroka **Hagaja**. Narod je izgradio svoje kuće, a Božji dom zaboravio. Zato *„sipaju u kesu, a prosipa im se”* i siju, a ne žanju. Blagoslov u vlastitim kesama dolazi kad se počne graditi Božji dom.
sections.subtitle_en: Only a believer gives to evangelization: Protestants, a diamond chalice, and old chairs
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matijašević compares Catholics and Protestants and speaks about a chalice
sections.content_en:
Matijašević points out the difference between humanitarian giving and giving for evangelization. **For a humanitarian purpose, anyone will give**, even an unbeliever when he sees a great need. For evangelization, only a believer will give, because to an unbeliever it means nothing.

In this, he also sees the reason why Protestants in the West are, as he says, more successful than Catholics. For Protestants, giving a tithe and investing in evangelization is a completely normal thing. Catholics, according to his words, would prefer everything to be a *"stable"*, so they immediately wonder why everything in the church is so expensive.

The guest thinks differently: *"Well, let things be expensive."* As an example, he takes the **chalice**. In it is the blood of Christ that saved the believer, so let it even be made of diamond, instead of an ordinary cup that some think is enough.

He also recounts an anecdote of a preacher who was furnishing a prayer hall. People were offering him chairs that they no longer needed at home, and he responded with a question: *"Those chairs are not good enough for your house, but they are good enough for God's house?"* In the end, new chairs were placed in the hall. The reason, says Matijašević, is that **God deserves the best** and that such an attitude shows how much a person cares.

At the end of the chapter, he refers to the prophet **Haggai**. The people built their houses, but forgot God's house. That is why *"they put into a purse, and it is scattered"* and they sow, but do not reap. The blessing in one's own purses comes when one begins to build God's house.

sections.subtitle: Organizator koji plaća vlastitu kotizaciju: „Stavi novac tamo gdje su ti usta”
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o tome kako je i sam plaćao kotizaciju za Eho konferenciju
sections.content:
Matijašević svoje stavove potkrepljuje osobnim primjerom. **Prvih nekoliko godina Eho konferencije**, koju je sam organizirao, plaćao je kotizaciju kao i svaki drugi polaznik.

Objašnjava da je bio stava kako od drugih ne može tražiti da plate ako to sam nije spreman učiniti: *„Ja sam prvi u tome, ja prvi želim biti, meni je stalo. Ne mogu očekivati od nekoga da uloži u nešto gdje ja nisam spreman isto uložiti.”* Načelo sažima poznatom izrekom: *stavi novac tamo gdje su ti usta*.

Gost zatim prepričava rečenicu jednog propovjednika koja mu se posebno svidjela. Propovjednik je, nakon što je sa slušateljima podijelio sve što je imao, rekao: *„Ako sad ne date, vi ste mene pokrali. Jer vi ste od mene primili, a niste ništa vratili.”*
sections.subtitle_en: An organizer who pays his own registration fee: „Put your money where your mouth is”
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about how he himself paid the registration fee for the Eho conference
sections.content_en:
Matijašević supports his views with a personal example. **For the first few years of the Eho conference**, which he organized himself, he paid the registration fee just like any other participant.

He explains that he held the stance that he could not ask others to pay if he was not ready to do so himself: *„I am the first in that, I want to be the first, I care. I cannot expect someone to invest in something where I am not ready to invest as well.”* He summarizes the principle with the well-known saying: *put your money where your mouth is*.

The guest then recounts a sentence from a preacher that he particularly liked. The preacher, after sharing everything he had with the listeners, said: *„If you do not give now, you have robbed me. Because you received from me, and you gave nothing back.”*

sections.subtitle: Korinćani ili Filipljani: Pavao i podrška onima koji služe Riječju
sections.screenshot_description: Matijašević uspoređuje Pavlov odnos prema Korinćanima i Filipljanima
sections.content:
Matijašević se osvrće na argument koji se, kako kaže, često koristi protiv plaćanja onih koji služe u Crkvi. Pavao je u Korintu sam izrađivao šatore i od Korinćana nije htio ništa uzeti. Gost odgovara protupitanjem: *„Jeste li sigurni da želite biti kao Korinćani?”*

Korinćane opisuje kao **nezrelu zajednicu**. Svađali su se oko toga tko je veći, na sastancima su se opijali i bludničili, a mučile su ih usporedbe i alkoholizam. Drugu poslanicu Korinćanima tumači kao Pavlov odgovor na prigovor da je u pismima prestrog, a uživo nije takav. Upravo zbog njihove nezrelosti Pavao im poručuje: *„Ove slave mi nećete oduzeti”*, i dolazi o vlastitom trošku.

S **Filipljanima** je bilo drukčije. Od njih je Pavao više puta primio pomoć. Njima je upućena molitva koju vjernici danas rado mole za financijski blagoslov: *„Bog moj pobrinut će se za svaku vašu potrebu raskošno prema bogatstvu svoje slave.”* Gost upozorava na kontekst: nekoliko redaka ranije Pavao zahvaljuje Filipljanima za podršku. Blagoslov je dakle molio za one koji su ga podržavali, a Korinćanima to nije rekao.

Matijašević navodi još dva mjesta:

- Pavlovo pitanje Korinćanima: ako je on njima sijao duhovna dobra, je li velika stvar ako od njih ubire materijalna?
- **Poslanicu Galaćanima**, za koju kaže da je ljudi zaboravljaju: onaj koji se poučava u Riječi neka dijeli svoja dobra s onim koji ga poučava.

*„Gdje je to danas?”*, pita se gost.
sections.subtitle_en: Corinthians or Philippians: Paul and support for those who serve with the Word
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matijašević compares Paul's attitude toward the Corinthians and the Philippians
sections.content_en:
Matijašević reflects on the argument that is, as he says, often used against paying those who serve in the Church. In Corinth, Paul made tents himself and did not want to take anything from the Corinthians. The guest responds with a counter-question: *“Are you sure you want to be like the Corinthians?”*

He describes the Corinthians as an **immature community**. They argued over who was greater, at meetings they got drunk and committed fornication, and they were troubled by comparisons and alcoholism. He interprets the Second Epistle to the Corinthians as Paul's response to the complaint that he is too strict in his letters, while not being like that in person. Precisely because of their immaturity, Paul tells them: *“You will not deprive me of this boast”*, and comes at his own expense.

With the **Philippians** it was different. From them, Paul received help multiple times. To them was addressed the prayer that believers readily pray today for financial blessing: *“My God will lavishly take care of your every need according to the riches of his glory.”* The guest warns of the context: a few lines earlier Paul thanks the Philippians for their support. Therefore, he prayed the blessing for those who supported him, and he did not say that to the Corinthians.

Matijašević cites two more places:

- Paul's question to the Corinthians: if he sowed spiritual goods among them, is it a great thing if he reaps material ones from them?
- The **Epistle to the Galatians**, which he says people forget: let the one who is taught in the Word share his goods with the one who teaches him.

*“Where is that today?”*, the guest wonders.

sections.subtitle: Isusova kesa, nardova pomast i konferencija od 25.000 eura
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o troškovima organizacije današnjih evangelizacijskih događaja
sections.content:
Matijašević odbacuje i tvrdnju da Isus ništa nije uzimao. Isus i učenici imali su zajedničku kesu, pa se gost pita od čega su živjeli: *„Nisu svaki put izvadili novac iz ribljih usta.”* Postojala je, dakle, neka podrška. Isus doduše nije nakon okupljanja skupljao milodar, ali nije ni imao iste uvjete kao današnji organizatori.

Te uvjete gost opisuje konkretnim brojkama. Organizacija konferencije može stajati, primjerice, **25.000 eura**. Netko će se ipak buniti: *„25 eura za slavljenje Boga?”* Matijašević odgovara da Boga svatko može slaviti kod kuće, besplatno, ali organizacija ima svoju cijenu. Vlasnik dvorane od 8.000 eura neće je ustupiti besplatno samo zato što će se u njoj slaviti Boga.

Takve izgovore uspoređuje s **Judom**, koji je prigovorio ženi što je prolila skupocjenu nardovu pomast umjesto da je proda i novac podijeli siromasima. Isus je odgovorio: *„Siromahe ćete uvijek imati.”* Gost napominje da je ta pomast vrijedila koliko jednogodišnja plaća.

Isto vrijedi i za apostole. Istina je da sami nisu imali ništa, ali ljudi su prodavali imanja i polagali im novac pred noge, a tim se novcem gradila Crkva. Današnji vjernici, zaključuje Matijašević, žele da im vjera rješava probleme, ali nisu spremni to isto podržati.
sections.subtitle_en: Jesus' purse, nard ointment, and a 25,000-euro conference
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the costs of organizing today's evangelization events
sections.content_en:
Matijašević also rejects the claim that Jesus took nothing. Jesus and the disciples had a common purse, so the guest asks what they lived on: *„They didn't pull money out of a fish's mouth every time.”* There was, therefore, some support. Jesus, to be sure, did not collect an offering after gatherings, but neither did he have the same conditions as today's organizers.

The guest describes these conditions with concrete numbers. Organizing a conference can cost, for example, **25,000 euros**. Someone will nevertheless protest: *„25 euros for praising God?”* Matijašević replies that anyone can praise God at home, for free, but organization has its price. The owner of an 8,000-euro hall will not give it for free just because God will be praised in it.

He compares such excuses to **Judas**, who reproached the woman for pouring out expensive nard ointment instead of selling it and distributing the money to the poor. Jesus answered: *„You will always have the poor.”* The guest notes that this ointment was worth as much as a year's salary.

The same applies to the apostles. It is true that they themselves had nothing, but people sold estates and laid the money at their feet, and with that money the Church was built. Today's believers, Matijašević concludes, want faith to solve their problems, but they are not ready to support that same thing.

sections.subtitle: Milost je besplatna, ali nije bezvrijedna: koljeno od pola milijuna i operacija od 5.000 eura
sections.screenshot_description: Matijašević prepričava primjer ozdravljenja nakon molitve
sections.content:
Na prigovor da se ne može naplaćivati nešto što je primljeno besplatno, Matijašević odgovara jasnim razlikovanjem. **Milost se ne može naplatiti, ali vrijeme može.** Mogao je biti negdje drugdje i zarađivati novac, a svoje je vrijeme posvetio ovoj službi. Onima koji ga podsjećaju da je i sam besplatno primio, s dozom ironije poručuje neka i oni odu i besplatno prime, pa neka rade isto što i on.

Poantu da besplatno ne znači bezvrijedno ilustrira s dva primjera:

- **Rukometaš Duvnjak** imao je, kako kaže, koljeno osigurano na pola milijuna eura. Gost se u šali pita: kad bi zajednica molila za njegovo bolesno koljeno i ono ozdravilo, bi li uplatio donaciju od pola milijuna? Sumnja u to, jer bi se tada i 500 eura činilo mnogo.
- **Stvarni slučaj s molitvenog susreta**: ženi s problemom diska u leđima nakon molitve se vratila mogućnost pokreta koji prije nije mogla izvesti. Mjesec dana kasnije stanje je i dalje bilo dobro. U isto vrijeme sestra jedne gostu poznate osobe, zbog neizdržive boli, platila je privatnu operaciju istog problema **5.000 eura**.

Matijašević se pita bi li donacija nakon takvog ozdravljenja bila blizu 5.000 eura koji bi ostali u džepu. Zaključuje da ne bi, i da bi se i 100 eura smatralo velikim darom, iako su ljudi spremni platiti mnogo da bi dobili zdravlje. Ono što je besplatno, ponavlja, ne znači da ništa ne vrijedi niti da se trud ne smije nagraditi, kako bi ljudi i dalje ustrajali u službi.
sections.subtitle_en: Grace is free, but it is not worthless: a half-million knee and a 5,000-euro surgery
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matijašević recounts an example of healing after prayer
sections.content_en:
To the objection that one cannot charge for something received freely, Matijašević responds with a clear distinction. **Grace cannot be charged for, but time can.** He could have been somewhere else earning money, yet he dedicated his time to this ministry. To those who remind him that he himself received freely, he remarks with a touch of irony that they too should go and receive freely, and then do the same as he does.

He illustrates the point that free does not mean worthless with two examples:

- **Handball player Duvnjak** had, as he says, his knee insured for half a million euros. The guest jokingly asks: if the community prayed for his sick knee and it was healed, would he make a donation of half a million? He doubts it, because then even 500 euros would seem like a lot.
- **A real case from a prayer meeting**: after prayer, a woman with a disc problem in her back regained the ability to make a movement she previously could not perform. A month later, her condition was still good. At the same time, the sister of a person known to the guest, due to unbearable pain, paid **5,000 euros** for private surgery for the same problem.

Matijašević wonders whether a donation after such a healing would be close to the 5,000 euros that would have remained in the pocket. He concludes that it would not be, and that even 100 euros would be considered a large gift, even though people are ready to pay a lot to obtain health. What is free, he repeats, does not mean that it is worth nothing, nor that effort should not be rewarded so that people may continue to persevere in ministry.

sections.subtitle: Novac kao test vjernosti: 20 kuna u crkvi, 100 kuna za rundu
sections.screenshot_description: Gost uspoređuje davanje u crkvi s plaćanjem računa u birtiji
sections.content:
Matijašević zaključuje da je **novac test naše vjernosti**. Odnos prema novcu i ono na što ga trošimo pokazuje što nam je važno i koliko zapravo vjerujemo Bogu.

Krunoslav se nadovezuje mišlju: *„Svemu znamo cijenu, ali ničemu ne znamo pravu vrijednost.”* Opisuje iskustvo s vlastitih konferencija. Ljudi se žale na cijenu, iako su postojale vrlo rane i rane prijave po nižim cijenama. Na pitanje gdje su bili pola godine ranije, odgovaraju da nisu znali, iako su događaj mogli pratiti. Mogućnosti se uvijek nude, kaže voditelj, a o vjernicima ovisi hoće li ih prihvatiti. Upravo to pokazuje koliko im je do nečega stalo.

Gost u tome vidi poznat obrazac: **novac u Crkvi uvijek ima puno veću težinu nego u birtiji**. Prisjeća se vremena kuna. Za 10 ili 20 kuna u crkvi ljudi će se pobrinuti da se vidi, pa će čak i dijete poslati da ubaci novac pred svima. Sto kuna za rundu u kafiću nije nikakav problem, a 20 kuna u crkvi smatra se velikim darom.

Davanje Bogu, objašnjava Matijašević, nije izraz njegove potrebe, nego **zahvalnosti**. Kod Židova je taj novac išao onima koji su Bogu služili, kako bi mogli nastaviti služiti, a darivatelj je time pokazivao zahvalnost za ono što je primio.
sections.subtitle_en: Money as a test of faithfulness: 20 kuna in church, 100 kuna for a round
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares giving in church with paying a bill in a pub
sections.content_en:
Matijašević concludes that **money is a test of our faithfulness**. The attitude toward money and what we spend it on shows what is important to us and how much we actually trust God.

Krunoslav follows up with the thought: *„We know the price of everything, but the true value of nothing.”* He describes the experience from his own conferences. People complain about the price, even though there were very early and early registrations at lower prices. To the question of where they were half a year earlier, they answer that they did not know, even though they could have followed the event. Opportunities are always offered, says the host, and it depends on the faithful whether they will accept them. That is precisely what shows how much they care about something.

The guest sees a familiar pattern in this: **money in the Church always carries much more weight than in a pub**. He recalls the time of the kuna. For 10 or 20 kuna in church, people will make sure it is seen, so they will even send a child to put in the money in front of everyone. One hundred kuna for a round in a café is no problem at all, while 20 kuna in church is considered a great gift.

Giving to God, Matijašević explains, is not an expression of His need, but of **gratitude**. Among the Jews, that money went to those who served God, so that they could continue to serve, and the giver thereby showed gratitude for what he had received.

sections.subtitle: Ne vlasnici, nego upravitelji: nove felge i deset eura donacije
sections.screenshot_description: Matijašević objašnjava da čovjek nije vlasnik novca, nego upravitelj
sections.content:
Temu financija Matijašević zaokružuje načelom koje smatra temeljnim: **čovjek nije vlasnik novca, nego upravitelj**. Upravlja onim što mu je povjereno, a pravi Vlasnik jednoga će ga dana pitati što je s tim učinio.

Odgovor mnogih vjernika gost slikovito karikira: *„Kupio sam nove felge. A onda sam tamo donirao deset eura i bio sam dobar vjernik.”* Krunoslav dodaje s ironijom: *„Valjaš, slugo dobri i vjerni”*, i primjećuje da si tako sami tepamo.

Matijašević pojašnjava da nema ništa protiv novih felgi. Važno mu je da omjer između onoga što je netko spreman uložiti u Božje stvari i onoga što ulaže u propadljivo bude barem približan.
sections.subtitle_en: Not owners, but stewards: new rims and a ten-euro donation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matijašević explains that man is not the owner of money, but a steward
sections.content_en:
Matijašević rounds off the topic of finances with a principle he considers fundamental: **man is not the owner of money, but a steward**. He manages what has been entrusted to him, and one day the true Owner will ask him what he did with it.

The guest vividly caricatures the response of many believers: *“I bought new rims. And then I donated ten euros over there and I was a good believer.”* Krunoslav adds with irony: *“Well done, good and faithful servant”*, and observes that this is how we flatter ourselves.

Matijašević clarifies that he has nothing against new rims. What matters to him is that the ratio between what someone is ready to invest in the things of God and what they invest in the perishable be at least approximate.

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: pastir zbog utjecaja, služenje kao preduvjet vodstva
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj postavlja prvo blic pitanje „radnik ili pastir”
sections.content:
Primjećujući da je vrijeme proletjelo, Krunoslav najavljuje završni **„ili-ili” izazov**. Gost bira jednu od dviju ponuđenih opcija, koje su ponekad namjerno kontroverzne, a uvijek može ponuditi i treću i kratko je obrazložiti.

**Radnik ili pastir?** Na pitanje o radniku na Božjoj njivi ili pastiru Matijašević prvo priznaje da mu je jednostavnije biti radnik. Radnik odradi svoj dio, a odgovornost je na nekom drugom. Ipak bira **pastira**, jer pastir vodi, upravlja i ima priliku utjecati na one koje vodi, kao i na one koji će dalje utjecati na druge. Pastir ima veću odgovornost, ali i više prostora za utjecaj. Krunoslav to sažima: po pitanju utjecaja, pastir.

**Voditi ljude ili služiti ljudima?** Gost bira **služenje**. Smatra da se ne može voditi bez služenja, jer vođa mora biti dostupan, a vodstvo uključuje mnogo toga što je zapravo služenje. Krunoslav dodaje da je to Isus pokazao svojim primjerom.
sections.subtitle_en: Quick-fire questions: shepherd because of influence, service as a prerequisite for leadership
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks the first quick-fire question „worker or shepherd”
sections.content_en:
Noticing that time has flown by, Krunoslav announces the final **„either-or” challenge**. The guest chooses one of the two offered options, which are sometimes intentionally controversial, and can always offer a third one and briefly explain it.

**Worker or shepherd?** To the question about a worker in God's field or a shepherd, Matijašević first admits that it is simpler for him to be a worker. A worker does his part, and the responsibility is on someone else. Nevertheless, he chooses **the shepherd**, because the shepherd leads, governs, and has the opportunity to influence those he leads, as well as those who will further influence others. A shepherd has greater responsibility, but also more room for influence. Krunoslav summarizes this: in terms of influence, the shepherd.

**Lead people or serve people?** The guest chooses **service**. He believes that one cannot lead without serving, because a leader must be accessible, and leadership includes much that is actually service. Krunoslav adds that Jesus showed this by his example.

sections.subtitle: Postojanost umjesto karizme i srce kralja Davida
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava zašto bira kralja Davida
sections.content:
**Karizma ili postojanost?** Iako dolazi iz karizmatskog pokreta i karizmatske zajednice, Matijašević bez dvojbe bira **postojanost**. Smatra da upravo ona danas nedostaje: *„Život nije samo jedna dobra duhovna obnova, život je goriti i ostati gorjeti do kraja.”*

**Kraljevstvo Božje ili kraljevstvo ovoga svijeta?** To pitanje Krunoslav sam naziva lakšim, a gost kratko odgovara: **Kraljevstvo Božje**.

**Sveti Josip ili kralj David?** Ovo je, kako je voditelj najavio, najteže pitanje. Nakon kraće stanke gost napominje da o svetom Josipu nema mnogo zapisa i bira **kralja Davida**: *„David je bio lik.”* Krunoslav dodaje da se David znao dobro pokajati. Matijašević se slaže, ali ističe nešto drugo: Davidu je srce baš gorjelo. Ne tvrdi da Josipu nije, ali među biblijskim likovima David se posebno ističe. Započeo je viziju gradnje doma Jahvina i bilo mu je stalo do toga. Unatoč trenucima slabosti i grijeha, iz njegovih se psalama vidi srce usmjereno prema Gospodinu.

Odgovor završava osobnom željom. Gledajući svoj život, Matijašević bi volio da i njegovo srce, unatoč svemu, gori za Božjom prisutnošću i njegovim domom.
sections.subtitle_en: Perseverance instead of charisma and the heart of King David
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains why he chooses King David
sections.content_en:
**Charisma or perseverance?** Although he comes from the charismatic movement and a charismatic community, Matijašević chooses **perseverance** without hesitation. He believes that it is precisely what is missing today: *“Life is not just one good spiritual renewal, life is to burn and remain burning until the end.”*

**The Kingdom of God or the kingdom of this world?** Krunoslav himself calls this question easier, and the guest answers briefly: **The Kingdom of God**.

**Saint Joseph or King David?** This is, as the host announced, the most difficult question. After a short pause, the guest notes that there are not many records about Saint Joseph and chooses **King David**: *“David was a character.”* Krunoslav adds that David knew how to repent well. Matijašević agrees, but emphasizes something else: David's heart truly burned. He does not claim that Joseph's did not, but among biblical figures David particularly stands out. He began the vision of building the house of Yahweh and cared about it. Despite moments of weakness and sin, his psalms show a heart directed toward the Lord.

The answer ends with a personal wish. Looking at his life, Matijašević would like his heart, despite everything, to burn for God's presence and His house.

sections.subtitle: Izazov za idući mjesec: zapisujte svaki pad u obrazac koji želite promijeniti
sections.screenshot_description: Marko Matijašević zadaje gledateljima izazov za sljedeći mjesec
sections.content:
Na kraju razgovora Krunoslav moli gosta da gledateljima zada izazov za idući mjesec. To može biti nešto korisno za partnerske odnose, obitelj ili posao, nešto što mu je trenutno na srcu.

Matijašević, koji je izazov u šali nazvao „zadaćom”, predlaže praktičnu vježbu u dva koraka:

- **Odaberite jedan obrazac ponašanja** koji želite mijenjati.
- **Svaki dan zapisujte** kad ste upali u taj obrazac.

Tek nakon toga treba tražiti **protuobrazac**, odnosno ponašanje prema kojem se želi ići. Prvi mjesec služi tome da se osvijesti svaki trenutak kad se čovjek nađe u starom obrascu, jer, kako kaže, *„dok ne skužimo što radimo, ne možemo ni ispravljati”*.

Vježba se može primijeniti na partnerski odnos, financije, posao ili odnose sa zaposlenicima i kolegama. Područje je nebitno, važno je pronaći ono što se želi promijeniti i bilježiti koliko često se u to pada. Izazov se nadovezuje na misao koju je gost iznio ranije u epizodi: djeca i drugi oko nas upijaju ono što mi jesmo, pa je rad na vlastitim obrascima stalna zadaća.
sections.subtitle_en: Challenge for next month: write down every fall into the pattern you want to change
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko Matijašević gives viewers a challenge for the next month
sections.content_en:
At the end of the conversation, Krunoslav asks the guest to give the viewers a challenge for next month. It can be something useful for partner relationships, family, or work, something that is currently on his heart.

Matijašević, who jokingly called the challenge „homework”, suggests a practical exercise in two steps:

- **Choose one pattern of behavior** that you want to change.
- **Write down every day** when you fell into that pattern.

Only after that should one seek a **counter-pattern**, that is, the behavior toward which one wants to go. The first month serves to become aware of every moment when a person finds oneself in the old pattern, because, as he says, *„until we realize what we are doing, we cannot even correct it”*.

The exercise can be applied to a partner relationship, finances, work, or relationships with employees and colleagues. The area is irrelevant; it is important to find what one wants to change and record how often one falls into it. The challenge builds on the thought the guest stated earlier in the episode: children and others around us absorb who we are, so working on one's own patterns is a constant task.

sections.subtitle: Cvijeće za godišnjicu, odjava i najava: sjećanje na oslobađanje Banovine
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj zahvaljuje gostu i šali se na račun godišnjice braka
sections.content:
Krunoslav zahvaljuje gostu na izdvojenom vremenu i šali se na račun činjenice, spomenute ranije u razgovoru, da Matijašević na dan **osme godišnjice braka** s Mirjanom gostuje u podcastu. Savjetuje mu da nakon snimanja otrči u cvjećarnu, ako još radi, i kupi cvijeće, kako kod kuće ne bi bilo problema. Gost uzvraća da danas to neće biti problem i zahvaljuje na pozivu.

Voditelj zatim zahvaljuje gledateljima što prate podcast **Redefinicija** i poziva ih da postanu članovi na **Patreonu**, gdje sljedeću epizodu mogu pogledati već danas. Emisija se zatvara pozdravom: *„Vidimo se u Redefiniciji.”*

Slijedi isječak iz sljedeće epizode. Sugovornik prepričava ratno sjećanje: izišao je van i pitao sprema li se nešto i kreće li se u oslobađanje. Kad je dobio potvrdan odgovor i savjet da se makne, u auto je stavio knjige, **župne matice** i ono što je imao te krenuo *„kao neki slalom između tenkova”* prema Zagrebu. Na putu od Siska prema selima čuo je početak kanonade. Bilo je to oko pet sati ujutro, kada je hrvatsko topništvo započelo pripremu za **oslobađanje Banovine**.
sections.subtitle_en: Flowers for an anniversary, sign-off and teaser: a memory of the liberation of Banovina
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host thanks the guest and jokes about his wedding anniversary
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav thanks the guest for taking the time and jokes about the fact, mentioned earlier in the conversation, that Matijašević is guesting on the podcast on the day of his **eighth wedding anniversary** with Mirjana. He advises him to run to a florist after the recording, if it is still open, and buy flowers so that there won't be problems at home. The guest replies that today that won't be a problem and expresses gratitude for the invitation.

The host then thanks the viewers for following the podcast **Redefinicija** and invites them to become members on **Patreon**, where they can watch the next episode as early as today. The show closes with the greeting: *„See you on Redefinicija.”*

A clip from the next episode follows. The speaker recounts a wartime memory: he went outside and asked whether something was being prepared and whether the move toward liberation was beginning. When he received an affirmative answer and the advice to move away, he put books, **parish registers**, and whatever he had into his car and set off *„like some slalom between the tanks”* toward Zagreb. On the way from Sisak toward the villages, he heard the beginning of the cannonade. It was around five o'clock in the morning, when the Croatian artillery began preparations for the **liberation of Banovina**.
